name: 通話で共有する音の選択グリッド
prompt:
Create a crisp flat Japanese sound-selection grid at exactly 390×258 pixels. Use reference image 1 as the exact source for native Japanese wording and layout. Use reference image 2 for the original screen style and reference image 3 for the six original icon illustrations. Keep the Japanese version and do not copy the English Discord branding or English labels.

At x16 y8 show ライトハウスの音 in 12px Meiryo Bold #1D1D1D. Arrange six equal cards exactly as in reference image 1: 110×92 at x16, x140, x264; first row y46, second row y150. Use the exact labels and order: アヒル, ホーン, 虫の音, 拍手, 残念な音, ドラム. Labels are 12px Meiryo Regular #1D1D1D; first row at y105 and second row at y209. Each card has a centered 32×38 icon area: x55/x179/x303 with y55 for the first row and y159 for the second.

Match the original icons from reference image 3 closely: a green-headed duck, metallic airhorn with blue sound-wave rings, brown cricket, yellow clapping hands with impact marks, gold trumpet/sad horn, and red drum with two sticks. Preserve the original emoji colors and silhouettes; do not substitute unrelated generic symbols. Use a small neutral light-gray circle behind each icon, matching the source.

Use a pure white page and white card fills. The first duck card is selected and has a thin solid green outline #047857; all other cards have a thin neutral gray outline #E8ECE9. Remove all mint/pale green card fills. Use modest rounded corners matching the native preview. No shadows, gradients, colored card fills, extra text, logos, outer frame or controls. There is no hyperlink text. Return only the flat 390×258 component.

review.feedback: User reported that the six icon illustrations do not match the original source; v002 replaces them with source pixels.

reviewNotes: User feedback revoked the v001 icon review: its six illustrations were approximations and did not match the original source. Superseded by v002, which composites the six original source icon crops. The v001 layout still has approximately 2–4px geometry drift.
